materials.label: Puzriš-Dagan livestock agency archive
materials.what_audience_follows: Thousands of surviving records let the audience follow livestock obligations becoming classifiable, authenticated and retrievable through officials, seals and archival procedure rather than through the tablet acting alone.
sequence: Livestock, taxation, royal gifts and diplomatic transfers generate individual administrative records.
Officials and sealing practices attach responsibility and authentication to those records.
Records accumulate into an archival system that can be grouped and retrieved across transactions.
The reconstructed agency makes obligations visible at institutional scale, while enforcement still belongs to people and authorities.

locators: §§1.2–1.5: reconstruction of the Puzriš-Dagan central livestock agency and archive of more than 13,500 tablets

limitations: This is a bounded Ur III royal-institution case, centuries after the origin of writing.
The archive is selective and reconstructed; do not present it as a literal inventory of one stockyard or an empire-wide norm.
Use it as a later test of the institutional-capacity feedback mechanism, not proof of that mechanism at Uruk.
